finding.text: Servex `close_task` files no waiting task. `Servex/TaskLoop.js:10` only imports OpenItems: `TaskLoop.write_line` (worktree `Servex/TaskLoop.js:526`) never calls `OpenItems.after_write`. So the `complete` and `closed_by` lines that `close_task` writes (`TaskLoop.js:514-516`) and Dropped's lines (`TaskLoop.js:103`) skip the rule. The requirement names `close_task` as a chokepoint. `Servex/readme.md`, `core/Task/readme.md`, `doc/completion.md` and the header of `Servex/OpenItems.js` all say this hook is in place.

`OpenItems.test.mjs` never tests the `close_task` path. That is why finding 1 passed with 23 green checks. Add a case: run `TaskLoop.close_task` on a record that has one open task and one done task, and expect exactly one `open-items`.

Some closing paths still write without passing through the rule, yet the `Servex/OpenItems.js:72-73` comment says every path does. `Server/PromptRecords.mjs:127` and `Server/CloseoutWalk.mjs:138` (`--apply` writes `stop` lines) call `fs.appendFileSync` directly. `RecordWriter.append_once` (append.mjs and StaleClose when Servex is down) also appends raw. Either route these writes through the rule, or list them in the comment and the docs as known gaps.

The session page's new Score stat was never seen working. `shots/session-1200-after-worktree.png` only shows "This is a worktree preview, which is not allowed to ask Servex for numbers" on the Report tab: no stats bar and no "needs review". The handover admits this in its last log line. Shoot a no-task session on the main site after merge and restart.

The shot set is short. There is no `ai-1200-before-main.png` and no `session-400-before-main.png`, so two of the asked before/after pairs at 400 and 1200 are missing. The `ai-400` pair shows no layout change.

There may be a cost on every close. `OpenItems.after_write` runs inside the synchronous `write_line` in Servex. For every stop or complete line, it replays the whole record twice, plus up to two more replays in `reach()` for each filing, and child records are read from disk synchronously. `session-e00f55c9/session.jsonl` is 3.7 MB, so one close there could block Servex for a noticeable time. Worth measuring once.

Two remaining callers show a null score as "0%" (no throw): `public/framework/ai/sessions/doc/variants/SegBar.js:13` and `Server/PromptTrace.mjs:49` both do `Math.round(x.completion * 100)`. Route them through `Task.show` if they ever get a session.

Part of `core/Task/readme.md` is now stale. The old `completion` bullet right after the new text (diff line 605) still says "or 1 when complete", which is now wrong for a session. The new "No silent endings" bullet also ends with the formula link and the "Test: completion.test.mjs. The older description follows." text that belongs to the bullet above it.

The core design follows the brief. `Task.mean`/`Task.show`, the null result only when `is_session`, `tally().unscored`, the deterministic `open-items` id, and leaving closeout tasks out of `score_parts`/`reopened`/`complete()` all match it, and every decision has a log line. `completion.test.mjs` (37), `OpenItems.test.mjs` (23) and `session-query.test.mjs` all pass in the worktree. A fresh agent could pick this up from `plan.md`, `session.jsonl` and this review.

Ask 2 is now off by default (`Servex/OpenItems.js:97`, `SERVEX_OPEN_ITEMS=on`), so no session closed under 100% files its waiting task until the owner says yes. Nothing asks the owner for that yes: neither this record nor the parent's `session.jsonl` has a `{"wait":{"on":"owner"}}` task for "switch SERVEX_OPEN_ITEMS on?" (the parent has one only for the twins fold, line 114). Under agents.md law 5, a question left in a log line is a dropped task. File one on the parent record, with the dry-run counts (2 would file, 79 needs review) and how to switch it on (where the env var is set for Servex).

`public/framework/core/Session/readme.md:39` is the SessionFolders API index, and it still lists `of, home, create, all, twins, owner` without the new `url(id)` / `SessionFolders.url_in(repo, id)` (`SessionFolders.mjs:350-358`). Those two are now how a node writer must build a session link, so the readme should name them. The header comment and `Servex/agents/doc/own-page.md` were updated; the module readme was not.

The flat-link half of this diff (AskIndex, RefineQueue, UndoneAsks, CardAsk, TagRouter, SessionFolders.url_in) is not in `requirements.md`, and this task's `session.jsonl` has no log line saying why it is here. Add one line, so a fresh agent knows it came from the one-folder rule and not from this brief. `Servex/ext/refine/VoicePage.js:37` and `Servex/agents/page_tools.js:201` still build `/framework/ai/sessions/${id}/`. Those are write paths that go through the redirect, not links in text, so they are probably fine, but say so.

The two docs give different costs for a closing line. `Servex/OpenItems.js:105` says "about 0.4-1.2 s" on the 3.7 MB record; `core/Task/doc/completion.md:394` and the review answer say 0.5-0.7 s. Use one measured number in both.

`core/Task/doc/completion.md:392` reads in a confusing order. It says "The rule itself (`Task#closeout_line`) is unchanged" and then "`Task#closeout_line` builds it…", and "Servex/OpenItems.js appends it right after any closing line" now contradicts the off-by-default sentence before it. Put the flag sentence last, or write "appends it (when on)". `core/Task/readme.md:404` names `doc/completion.md` as plain text, not a link.

`SessionFolders.url` (`SessionFolders.mjs:351`) takes the first `/public/` in the absolute path. A checkout under a parent folder named `public` (say `C:/x/public/monorepo/`) would then give a wrong url. Matching the last `/public/` (or using `path.relative` against `<repo>/public`) avoids that.

The before/after shots from the first review are still incomplete. `shots/` has no `ai-1200-before-main.png` and no `session-400-before-main.png`, and the answer "mastermind shoots after merge" has no task on any record. This diff changes no page, so it doesn't block this landing.

The rest checks out. In the worktree, `Servex/OpenItems.test.mjs` passes 34 checks (section 9 covers the switch both ways, and shows the dry run writing nothing), `SessionFolders.test.mjs` passes 36 and `completion.test.mjs` passes 38. `after_write` gets its default from `this.on` on every call, and the two chokepoints call it with no option, so the flag works everywhere. The plan/write split is the simplest way to build the switch. The owner's "behaviour changes proposed with a dry-run first" is recorded in the parent's session.jsonl line 106.
